skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Guides AI agents to create distinctive, production-ready frontend interfaces with clear design direction.
skill.summary: Create memorable frontend UI with a defined aesthetic, feasibility scoring, and working implementation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives. The two Ruby backtick alerts match Markdown code fences around a DFII formula, and the blocker alerts match frontend design prose rather than reconnaissance. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe automation was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: * Avoid system fonts and AI-defaults (Inter, Roboto, Arial, etc.)

finding_verdicts.reason: The detected text is an opening Markdown code fence before a DFII scoring formula. It does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or any external process.
The detected text is a closing Markdown code fence after a design scoring formula. No shell backtick execution or command invocation is present.
The line tells the designer to avoid generic UI patterns. It is product design guidance, not system reconnaissance or environment probing.
The line advises against default fonts in generated frontend designs. It does not request host, filesystem, network, or system inspection.
The line is color palette guidance for interface design. It contains no instruction to enumerate or inspect the runtime system.
The line recommends an intentional visual composition choice. It is unrelated to reconnaissance, privilege discovery, or collection of local system details.

content.value_statement: Generic interface prompts often produce safe, forgettable screens. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to define a strong design direction, score feasibility, and implement production-ready UI.
actual_capabilities: Defines an explicit aesthetic direction before frontend implementation begins.
Scores design concepts with the Design Feasibility and Impact Index.
Guides typography, color, spacing, motion, texture, and depth decisions.
Requires working HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or framework code as output.
Promotes accessible, performant, semantic, and maintainable frontend implementation.
Provides a structured output format for design rationale and implementation.
limitations: Requires enough product, audience, and brand context to choose an appropriate direction.
Does not replace browser testing, accessibility audits, or product review.
May need adaptation for strict brand systems or regulated interface standards.
Focuses on web frontend work, not native mobile or backend architecture.

use_cases.title: Create a memorable landing page
use_cases.description: Turn a basic product brief into a strong visual direction and working frontend implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve an internal product screen
use_cases.description: Refine dense dashboards with clearer hierarchy, purposeful spacing, and accessible interaction states.

use_cases.title: Prototype a coded design system
use_cases.description: Translate a chosen aesthetic into reusable frontend rules for typography, color, motion, and layout.

prompt_templates.title: Start a design direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new page or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-design skill for a pricing page. Define the audience, aesthetic direction, DFII score, and the first implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build a distinctive screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for coded UI output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a working frontend screen for a productivity app. Avoid default SaaS patterns and include the design system snapshot before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing interface
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for improving current UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing dashboard concept with the frontend-design skill. Keep the workflow clear, but make the visual language more memorable and cohesive.

prompt_templates.title: Create a scalable visual system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a multi-screen product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scalable frontend direction for an analytics product. Include reusable typography, color, spacing, motion rules, and component behavior across three screens.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a landing page for an AI research notebook.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an editorial research-lab direction, a DFII score, a design system snapshot, and a working page implementation plan.

output_examples.input: A user asks to make a dashboard less generic.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies weak default patterns, proposes a stronger hierarchy, and explains the visual anchor that makes the screen recognizable.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a component library style direction.
output_examples.output: The skill defines fonts, color variables, spacing rhythm, motion limits, and guidance for accessible reusable components.

best_practices: Provide audience, product goal, brand constraints, and required screens before asking for implementation.
Ask for the DFII score and design system snapshot before accepting generated code.
Validate generated UI in a browser for responsiveness, accessibility, and performance.
anti_patterns: Using the skill without product context, audience context, or success criteria.
Accepting decorative effects that do not support the selected aesthetic direction.
Skipping accessibility, responsive layout, and performance checks after code generation.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create distinctive web interfaces with a clear design direction and working frontend implementation guidance.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to produce real HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or framework code, but users should still test the result.

faq.question: Can it work with React?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes React guidance and favors functional components with composable styles.

faq.question: Is it only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can support dashboards, product screens, components, and design system direction for web interfaces.

faq.question: Does it replace a designer?
faq.answer: No. It supports design thinking and implementation, but expert review is still useful for brand and user research.

faq.question: What inputs make it work best?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, product purpose, desired tone, brand constraints, and any technical framework requirements.
